column4: On the decks of the yachts moored off Bembridge, teak has long been the timber underfoot, chosen because its own natural oils let it shrug off salt spray and rain. That same quality is why it went ashore into English gardens, and why it suits a seat left out through the summer.¶¶This two-seat loveseat is built from solid teak, with broad arms that curve gently down toward the front and a back of close-set slats behind two plump back cushions. The seat cushions are thick and squared, covered in a weatherproof outdoor fabric that sheds rain and holds its colour, with covers that go straight in the washing machine. Left untreated, the frame will age to a soft silver; given a teak protector now and then, it keeps its honey tone.¶¶Set it under a porch roof or along the edge of a deck, facing whatever view you have. It is the right size for two people and a pot of coffee on a Sunday morning, or for one person stretched out sideways with a paperback. This listing is for one loveseat.

column7: Outdoor cushions¶The outdoor fabric resists water and sun, but cushions last longest when they are kept dry. The covers are machine washable; follow the care label. In the off season, bring cushions in or store them somewhere dry.¶¶Teak frame¶Left untreated, teak weathers naturally to a soft silver-grey. column7: Outdoor cushions¶The outdoor fabric resists water and sun, but cushions last longest when they are kept dry. column7: Outdoor cushions¶After rain, stand the cushions on edge so water drains away and air reaches both faces, and let them dry right through before sitting. To clean, wash it with mild soapy water and a soft brush, working along the grain, then rinse and let it dry. Do not use a pressure washer, which raises the grain. If you prefer to keep the honey colour, a teak protector or sealer can be applied; this is optional, never required.¶¶Glides¶The feet sit on non-marking plastic glides. Avoid wrapping them tightly in plastic, which traps moisture.¶¶A Note on Natural Variation¶Teak is a natural material, and every piece differs in grain, colour and the odd small knot or mineral streak. These differences, and the way the wood mellows outdoors, are part of its character.

column3: Settle in and make the most of time outside with the Kona Outdoor Patio Corner Modular Sofa. column4: Ericeira faces west over the Atlantic, and on summer evenings the town turns out along its cliff-top walls to watch the sun go down into the sea. Seating that wraps a corner suits a place built around a view, because everyone gets a good angle on it.¶¶Five pieces in solid teak lock together into an L with two sides of equal length: a left-arm chair, an armless seat, a corner seat, a second armless seat and a right-arm chair. Teak's own oils let it shrug off rain, and plastic glides under each foot keep deck boards unmarked. Assembly is straightforward.¶¶Fit it into the corner of a deck or a walled terrace, angled toward the garden or the water, with a low table in the crook of the L for a pot of coffee or a bowl of olives. Pull the pieces apart for a party and push them back together after. This set includes a left-arm chair, two armless chairs, a corner chair and a right-arm chair.

The frame is solid teak; seat and back cushions are covered in an outdoor fabric that stands up to sun, rain, stains and fading, and the covers are removable. Plastic glides sit under the legs, it is rated to 497 lbs, and assembly is simple.¶¶Pair it with the right-arm chair for a two-seat sofa on a small balcony, or add armless and corner seats to build a long sofa down the side of a deck. Alone, it is a comfortable single chair for a porch corner. This listing is for one left-arm chair.

column7: Outdoor cushions¶Let cushions dry fully after rain, and stand them on edge so water drains out. Blot spills straight away, then clean with mild soap and water and rinse. Bring them in, or store them in a dry place, through the off season. The covers are removable.¶¶Teak frame¶Teak's natural oils let it live outdoors. Left untreated, it weathers over time to a soft silver-grey; a teak protector or sealer, applied as its label directs, can hold the warmer tone if you prefer it, but is never required. To clean, wash with mild soapy water and a soft brush, rinse and let it dry. Never use a pressure washer, which raises the grain. On darker finishes, sun and rain gradually soften and lighten the colour.¶¶Glides¶Check the plastic glides now and then and keep them clean of grit, so the piece slides without marking deck boards, stone or tile.¶¶Seasonal storage¶In harsh winter weather, cover the piece with a breathable cover or store it somewhere dry and airy. Bring cushions indoors for the off season.¶¶A Note on Natural Variation¶Teak is a natural material, and grain, tone and small knots vary from board to board and piece to piece. As it weathers, colour shifts gradually; this is part of the character of the wood.
